metadata.title: Learning Representations by Back-Propagating Errors
metadata.source_note: Extracted from PDF->text fallback; .tex source not available. Math fidelity reduced.

nodes.name: Layered feed-forward network
nodes.statement: A network with a layer of input units at the bottom, any number of intermediate (hidden) layers, and a layer of output units at the top; connections within a layer or from higher to lower layers are forbidden, but connections may skip intermediate layers.
nodes.statement_clean: A directed acyclic neural network with input, hidden, and output layers; connections only go from lower to higher layers.

nodes.name: Hidden unit
nodes.statement: A unit that is not part of the input or output layers and whose desired state is not specified by the task; it must come to represent features of the task domain captured by the learned weights.
nodes.statement_clean: An internal network unit whose target activations are not directly supplied by training data.

nodes.name: Bias as extra weight
nodes.statement: A unit's bias is implemented by introducing an extra input that always has value $1$; the weight on that extra input is the bias and is equivalent to a threshold of opposite sign, treated like any other weight.
nodes.statement_clean: Biases are absorbed as weights from a constant input of $1$.

nodes.name: Total input to a unit
nodes.statement: $x_j = \sum_i y_i w_{ji}$
nodes.statement_clean: Each unit's total input is the weighted sum of the outputs of units in the layer below.
nodes.notes: Weights $w_{ji}$ connect lower-layer unit $i$ to upper-layer unit $j$; $y_i$ are the lower-layer outputs.

nodes.name: Logistic activation
nodes.statement_clean: A unit's output is the logistic (sigmoid) of its total input.

nodes.name: Total squared error
nodes.statement: $E = \tfrac{1}{2} \sum_c \sum_j (y_{j,c} - d_{j,c})^2$
nodes.statement_clean: Total error is half the sum of squared deviations between actual and desired output activations, summed over output units $j$ and training cases $c$.

nodes.name: Output-layer error derivative
nodes.statement: $\partial E / \partial y_j = y_j - d_j$
nodes.statement_clean: For an output unit, the partial derivative of the (per-case) error with respect to its activation is the actual minus the desired output.

nodes.name: Activation-to-input derivative (sigmoid)
nodes.statement: $\partial E / \partial x_j = \partial E / \partial y_j \cdot y_j (1 - y_j)$
nodes.statement_clean: The error gradient with respect to a unit's total input equals the gradient w.r.t. its output times the sigmoid derivative $y_j(1-y_j)$.

nodes.name: Weight-gradient formula
nodes.statement: $\partial E / \partial w_{ji} = \partial E / \partial x_j \cdot y_i$
nodes.statement_clean: The gradient with respect to a weight equals the upstream input-error times the activation of the source unit.

nodes.name: Backward propagation across a layer
nodes.statement: $\partial E / \partial y_i = \sum_j \partial E / \partial x_j \cdot w_{ji}$
nodes.statement_clean: The error gradient at a hidden unit's output is the weighted sum of the input-error gradients of all units it feeds, weighted by the corresponding connection weights.

nodes.name: Gradient-descent weight update
nodes.statement: $\Delta w = -\varepsilon\, \partial E / \partial w$
nodes.statement_clean: Each weight is changed by an amount proportional to (the negative of) the accumulated error gradient.

nodes.name: Momentum (acceleration) update
nodes.statement: $\Delta w(t) = -\varepsilon\, \partial E / \partial w(t) + \alpha\, \Delta w(t-1)$
nodes.statement_clean: An acceleration / momentum rule: the current weight change is the gradient term plus an exponentially-decayed contribution of the previous change.
nodes.notes: $t$ is incremented by $1$ for each sweep through the input-output set; $\alpha \in (0,1)$ is the momentum factor.

nodes.name: Learning representations in hidden units
nodes.statement: Find a synaptic-modification rule that lets an arbitrarily connected neural network develop an internal structure (representations in hidden units) appropriate for a task specified only by desired output vectors for given input vectors.
nodes.statement_clean: How should hidden units be configured so that a feed-forward network produces the desired input-output mapping?

nodes.name: Minimize total error $E$ over weights
nodes.statement: Minimize the total squared error $E = \tfrac{1}{2} \sum_c \sum_j (y_{j,c} - d_{j,c})^2$ over the network's weights $\{w_{ji}\}$ by gradient descent.
nodes.statement_clean: Optimization formulation: minimize squared output error over the weight vector.

nodes.name: Back-propagation
nodes.statement: Two-pass procedure that computes $\partial E / \partial w_{ji}$ for every weight in a layered network: a forward pass propagates activations bottom-up using $(1)$-$(2)$, and a backward pass propagates error derivatives top-down using $(4)$-$(7)$, after which weights are updated by $(8)$ or $(9)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Compute weight gradients via a forward activation pass and a backward error-derivative pass, then update weights by gradient descent.
input: Training set of input-output cases $\{(x_c, d_c)\}$

nodes.name: Initialize weights
nodes.statement: Set the weights to small random values to break symmetry (e.g. uniform on $[-0.3, 0.3]$ in the symmetry experiment).

nodes.name: Forward pass
nodes.statement: Present an input vector and propagate activations layer-by-layer using $x_j = \sum_i y_i w_{ji}$ and $y_j = 1/(1+e^{-x_j})$ until the output layer is reached.

nodes.name: Output-layer error derivatives
nodes.statement: For each output unit $j$ compute $\partial E / \partial y_j = y_j - d_j$.

nodes.name: Backward pass through hidden layers
nodes.statement: Propagate derivatives top-down: at each unit $j$, $\partial E / \partial x_j = \partial E / \partial y_j \cdot y_j(1-y_j)$, then for each unit $i$ in the layer below set $\partial E / \partial y_i = \sum_j \partial E / \partial x_j \cdot w_{ji}$.

nodes.name: Compute weight gradients
nodes.statement: For every weight set $\partial E / \partial w_{ji} = \partial E / \partial x_j \cdot y_i$.

nodes.name: Update weights (gradient descent)
nodes.statement: Either change $w$ after every case, or accumulate $\partial E / \partial w$ over all cases and apply $\Delta w = -\varepsilon\, \partial E / \partial w$, optionally with momentum $\Delta w(t) = -\varepsilon\, \partial E / \partial w(t) + \alpha\, \Delta w(t-1)$.

nodes.name: Iterate over sweeps
nodes.statement: Repeat the forward and backward passes over the training set for many sweeps until $E$ is acceptably small.

nodes.name: Mirror-symmetry detection
nodes.statement: A network with $6$ input units, $2$ hidden units, and $1$ output unit learns to detect whether the binary input vector is symmetric about its centre point; trained for $1{,}425$ sweeps over $64$ patterns with $\varepsilon = 0.1$, $\alpha = 0.9$, weights initialized uniformly in $[-0.3, 0.3]$.
nodes.statement_clean: A 6-2-1 network learns mirror symmetry; the two hidden units develop weights symmetric about the input midpoint with magnitudes in ratio $1{:}2{:}4$.
nodes.notes: Demonstrates that hidden units develop interpretable, distributed features.

nodes.name: Family-tree relationships
nodes.statement: A five-layer network learns triples $\langle\text{person 1}\rangle\langle\text{relationship}\rangle\langle\text{person 2}\rangle$ from two isomorphic family trees (English and Italian); trained for $1{,}500$ sweeps on $100$ of the $104$ triples with $\varepsilon = 0.005$, $\alpha = 0.5$ (then $\varepsilon = 0.01$, $\alpha = 0.9$) and weight-decay $0.2\%$, and generalizes correctly to the four held-out triples.
nodes.statement_clean: A deep network learns to complete kinship triples and discovers distributed representations (e.g. nationality, generation, family branch) in its hidden units.
nodes.notes: Demonstrates generalization from learned distributed representations.

nodes.name: Recurrent (synchronous iterative) net
nodes.statement: A synchronous iterative net run for three iterations is mapped to an equivalent layered net by unrolling in time; the constraint that corresponding weights in different layers stay equal is preserved by averaging $\partial E / \partial w$ over copies before updating.
nodes.statement_clean: Back-propagation extends to recurrent nets via unrolling in time with weight-sharing across the time-replicated layers.

nodes.name: Choice of nonlinearity is flexible
nodes.statement: It is not necessary to use exactly $(1)$ and $(2)$: any input-output function with a bounded derivative will do, but combining inputs linearly before applying the nonlinearity simplifies learning.
nodes.statement_clean: Equations (1)-(2) are convenient but not required; any smooth bounded nonlinearity works.

nodes.name: Symmetry breaking by random initialization
nodes.statement: Weights are initialized to small random values to break symmetry, otherwise hidden units that start identical would receive identical updates and remain functionally indistinguishable.
nodes.statement_clean: Random initialization is needed so different hidden units can specialize.

nodes.name: Local minima rarely a problem in practice
nodes.statement: Although the error surface may contain local minima so that gradient descent is not guaranteed to find a global optimum, experience on many tasks shows that networks with more than the minimum number of connections rarely get stuck in poor local minima; extra dimensions provide paths around barriers.
nodes.statement_clean: In practice, over-parameterized networks avoid bad local minima.

nodes.name: Biological implausibility
nodes.statement: The learning procedure as stated is not a plausible model of learning in brains, but its success motivates searching for biologically plausible mechanisms of gradient descent in weight-space.
nodes.statement_clean: Back-propagation is not biologically realistic but suggests fruitful directions.

nodes.name: Independent discovery
nodes.statement: Variants of the learning procedure were discovered independently by David Parker (personal communication) and by Yann Le Cun.
nodes.statement_clean: Parker and Le Cun independently developed similar procedures.

nodes.name: Why hidden units are needed for symmetry
nodes.statement: Symmetry detection cannot be performed by directly connecting input units to the output unit because individual input units carry no evidence of symmetry; intermediate units are essential (a more formal proof appears in ref. 2).
nodes.statement_clean: Detecting parity-like properties such as symmetry provably requires hidden units.

nodes.name: Perceptron-convergence procedure (cited)
nodes.statement: The classical perceptron-convergence procedure learns a separating weight vector when input units are directly connected to output units, but cannot learn appropriate hidden-unit representations.
nodes.statement_clean: Perceptron learning works only for direct input-output connections, not for networks with hidden layers.
